LESSON: PHONOLOGICAL SPEAKING

Grade: Grade 2
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.3: Phonological SPEAKING

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Phonological SPEAKING. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Which words contain 4 lessons letter-sounds to make  Learners blend syllables to form words and these sounds?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. recognize and say multiple groups
2. use appropriate words to games to enable them to listen to different make short, meaningful sounds sentences  Learners give words that rhyme
3. appreciate the role of  Learners are guided to make a list of all the blending and segmenting in sounds they can hear from the forming sentences environment(My home, my community)

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: PHONOLOGICAL SPEAKING
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Phonological SPEAKING helps you succeed in LITERACY ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: PHONOLOGICAL SPEAKING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Recognize and say multiple groups

What this means
In this part you learn to recognize and say multiple groups. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recognize and say multiple groups.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Phonological SPEAKING”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recognize and say multiple groups. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use appropriate words to games to enable them to listen to different make short, meaningful sounds sentences  Learners give words that rhyme

What this means
In this part you learn to use appropriate words to games to enable them to listen to different make short, meaningful sounds sentences  Learners give words that rhyme. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use appropriate words to games to enable them to listen to different make short, meaningful sounds sentences  Learners give words that rhyme.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Phonological SPEAKING to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use appropriate words to games to enable them to listen to different make short, meaningful sounds sentences  Learners give words that rhyme. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the role of  Learners are guided to make a list of all the blending and segmenting in sounds they can hear from the forming sentences environment(My home, my community)

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of  Learners are guided to make a list of all the blending and segmenting in sounds they can hear from the forming sentences environment(My home, my community). You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of  Learners are guided to make a list of all the blending and segmenting in sounds they can hear from the forming sentences environment(My home, my community).
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of  Learners are guided to make a list of all the blending and segmenting in sounds they can hear from the forming sentences environment(My home, my community). Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Phonological SPEAKING is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Phonological SPEAKING”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: recognize and say multiple groups)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Phonological SPEAKING to a partner. (skill: use appropriate words to games to enable them to listen to different make short, meaningful sounds sentences  Learners give words that rhyme)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the role of  Learners are guided to make a list of all the blending and segmenting in sounds they can hear from the forming sentences environment(My home, my community))

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Phonological SPEAKING to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: recognize and say multiple groups.
3. Practise this skill: use appropriate words to games to enable them to listen to different make short, meaningful sounds sentences  Learners give words that rhyme.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of  Learners are guided to make a list of all the blending and segmenting in sounds they can hear from the forming sentences environment(My home, my community).
5. Make one local Kenya example of Phonological SPEAKING from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Phonological SPEAKING: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 2 learner study Phonological SPEAKING?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which words contain 4 lessons letter-sounds to make  Learners blend syllables to form words and these sounds?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Phonological SPEAKING means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: recognize and say multiple groups.
5. Be able to: use appropriate words to games to enable them to listen to different make short, meaningful sounds sentences  Learners give words that rhyme.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
